title: Review: Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading (VPIN), Market Volatility, and High-Frequency Liquidity (Retest as a POWER if it is about the next
body: FRAGILE (Claude, 2026-10-25). rank(vrp,30) -> tail_day: no leak (all inputs known at the close, target is the next session). But the skill is thin (+1.2%) and lives in 2017-20: tested on 2021+ only it drops to +0.2%. It adds nothing on top of the plain 'implied move vs 20-day range' (impl/rng20 alone: +6.3%, 9/9 years; vrp on top of it: -0.07%). VPIN itself was never measured - vrp is a loose stand-in.

title: Review: On days where gex_rank < 0.2 (low dealer gamma) does the absolute NQ range (y_high - y_low) exceed the median range of all days by a statistically sig
body: CONFIRMED (already known) (Claude, 2026-10-25). Low dealer gamma -> wider NQ ranges is real: on the range scaled by its 20-day norm gex_rank gives +7.5% skill, 9/9 unseen years, and +6.1% on top of k_range20. No leak. But gex_rank is already one of the brain's base inputs, so this is the known gamma edge rediscovered; nothing new to ship. On the raw (unscaled) range the 2021+ skill is only +0.1% - the scaled form is the honest one.

title: Review: When the NQ opens near the high of the Asian session (k_open_vs_asia = 1), are we more likely to break yesterday's high during the NY session?
body: CONFIRMED (fact, no new information) (Claude, 2026-10-25). True in both halves (+11.9% / +15.4%), no leak - the open is known when the question starts. But it is a stand-in for where the open sits versus yesterday's high: k_open_vs_yday alone gives +48% skill, and k_open_vs_asia adds -0.05% on top. Part of it is by definition: an open already above yesterday's high counts as 'took it'. Fine as a morning-read line, not an edge.

title: Review: Selling a same-day iron condor pays when the realized move stays inside the options-priced move; my memory has only daily close-to-close returns and d
body: CONFIRMED (mechanical) (Claude, 2026-10-25). rank(impl/rng,252) -> inside_day holds in both halves (2021+: +4.0%, 5/5 years) and survives window nudges (200/300 days). No leak (target aligned to the next session; checked against the session table, 97% agreement). The mechanism is simple: a wide day relative to tomorrow's expected move contains tomorrow. rng20/rng alone does as well (+3.5%); the options-implied part adds only +0.4% (5/9 years). Possibly useful context for short-premium days, but no new information beyond range mean-reversion.

title: Review: Do days with higher SPX dealer gamma exposure (k_spx_gex) tend to have a relatively smaller NQ intraday range (y_range) compared to its 20‑day average
body: FRAGILE (Claude, 2026-10-25). k_spx_gex starts in 2019, so only 5 unseen years (4/5 better). It adds +1.5% over QQQ gex_rank, but only +0.15% once the implied move vs the 20-day range is included (impl/rng20 alone: +26% skill on this target). No leak, sensible direction (more dealer gamma = calmer day), but too little history to say it adds anything to what the brain already uses.

title: Review: Do larger overnight gaps (k_gap) increase the probability that NQ closes above yesterday's high (y_closed_above_yday_high)?
body: CONFIRMED (fact, no new information) (Claude, 2026-10-25). True in both halves (+14.2% / +14.0%), no leak. Mechanical: a big gap up opens near or above yesterday's high, so closing above it is easier. k_open_vs_yday alone does better (+26.6%) and k_gap adds -0.04% on top (corr 0.73). A fact, not an edge.
